nodes.content: Design a persistent ordered index supporting online key-range repartitioning without blocking snapshot scans or compromising crash recovery.
requirements: Concurrent updates, repartitioning, and crashes preserve committed writes and snapshot-consistent, duplicate-free range scans.
During repartitioning, p99 operation latency stays within 2× the same workload’s non-repartitioning baseline.

nodes.content: Use MVCC B+tree shards, epoch-pinned scan routing, WAL-logged update deltas during bounded background copying, and atomic partition-map cutover.
How can partition splits retain committed writes and duplicate-free snapshot scans through crashes and atomic cutover?
Epoch-pinned scans and WAL-ordered delta replay prevent lost commits, snapshot anomalies, and duplicate keys across crash-injected cutovers.
Specify WAL commit ordering, replay and epoch lifetimes; implement durable map cutover, then crash-test snapshot scans and updates.
Run SplitCrash-1: inject crashes at 12 WAL/cutover boundaries under concurrent updates; compare recovered keys and pinned scans against MVCC oracle.
SplitCrash-1: 120,000 crash-injected runs across 12 boundaries yielded zero lost committed writes or snapshot-scan mismatches against the MVCC oracle.
Retain epoch-pinned routing and WAL-ordered replay for cutover correctness; SplitCrash-1 found no recovery or snapshot violations.
SplitCrash-1 harness includes 12 crash hooks, durable-WAL replay fixtures, and MVCC-oracle checks for recovered keys and snapshot scans.
On the retained cutover design, mutation-test SplitCrash-1 with dropped WAL records and duplicate scan keys; require 100% detection.
SplitCrash-1 caught all 48 injected WAL-loss and duplicate-scan mutants, strengthening correctness evidence for epoch-pinned, WAL-replayed cutovers.
A durable cutover fence and per-key LSN deduplication preserve committed writes and duplicate-free epoch-pinned scans after repeated crashes.
Extend SplitCrash-1 with double crashes at cutover fences and duplicate per-key LSN replay; verify writes and scans against MVCC oracle.
SplitCrash-1 found duplicate scan keys in 23/20,000 double-crash runs: fence replay exposed both parent and child ranges.
Retain epoch-pinned WAL replay, but require recovered scans to select one partition-map generation; per-key deduplication missed duplicate ranges.
Throttle repartition copying with 256-key batches and feedback from rolling p99 latency, reserving foreground update and scan capacity.
Measure mixed-workload p99 against baseline; tune 256-key copier throttling to ≤2×, then rerun crash-injected snapshot checks.
Run MixSplit-10M (70/30 updates/scans), tune 256-key copier throttling against baseline p99, then verify crashed snapshots with SplitCrash-1.
MixSplit-10M benchmark bundle contains baseline and repartition p99 traces, 256-key copier settings, and SplitCrash-1 snapshot-check logs.
Can 256-key feedback throttling keep MixSplit-10M update and scan p99 ≤2× baseline without starving split completion?
Feedback-throttled 256-key copying holds MixSplit-10M p99 ≤1.8× baseline for updates and scans while completing splits within 90 seconds.
Reproduce MixSplit-10M bundle over 30 splits; compare update/scan p99 against baseline and record 256-key copier completion times.
Across 30 MixSplit-10M splits, update and scan p99 reached 1.64× and 1.72× baseline; slowest split completed in 83 seconds.
Adopt feedback-throttled 256-key copying: MixSplit-10M p99 stayed below 1.8× baseline and all 30 splits finished within 83 seconds.
With adopted throttling, crash-test MixSplit-10M map-generation cutovers; compare recovered writes and scans to the MVCC oracle and p99 to baseline.
In 10,000 crash-injected cutovers, recovered writes/scans matched the oracle; post-restart split scan p99 reached 2.3× baseline despite throttling.
Can feedback-throttled copying keep post-restart scan p99 ≤2× baseline when WAL replay and foreground scans contend?
Sweep copier pauses and WAL-replay I/O caps on post-restart MixSplit-10M; measure scan p99 and split completion against baseline.
Post-restart MixSplit-10M scan p99 remained 2.12× baseline even with copying paused; WAL replay saturated shared read I/O.
After mandatory recovery, reserve 75% read I/O for scans, cap resumed split-delta replay at 25%, and defer cutover.
For uncutover splits, recovered parent shards contain every committed write and support snapshots while child-delta replay is paused.
Can restarted uncutover splits serve every committed version from parent shards while child replay remains paused?
Crash 5,000 uncutover MixSplit-10M splits; pause child replay, then compare parent-served snapshot scans and committed writes against MVCC oracle.
In 17/5,000 paused-child-replay restarts, parent scans missed committed updates stored only in unreplayed child deltas.
Audit WAL commit LSNs and parent-versus-child routing for the 17 misses; independently verify parent visibility at restart.
WAL audit found all 17 commits in parent redo; completing mandatory parent recovery restored snapshot matches with child replay paused.
After mandatory parent recovery, can 75/25 scan/replay I/O reservation restore post-restart p99 below 2× without starving cutover?
After mandatory parent recovery, rerun 17 misses against oracle; benchmark MixSplit-10M with 75/25 scan/replay I/O for p99 and cutover.
All 17 recovered scans matched oracle; 75/25 I/O yielded post-restart scan p99 1.89× baseline, with slowest cutover at 104 seconds.
Require mandatory parent redo before applying 75/25 scan/replay I/O; redo resolved 17 misses, and restart scan p99 reached 1.89×.
Combine epoch-pinned single-generation routing, mandatory parent redo, 256-key throttled copying, and 75/25 post-restart scan/replay I/O reservations.
Can repeated crashes during 75/25 child replay preserve single-generation scans and restart scan p99 ≤2× baseline?
Mandatory parent redo and single-generation routing keep repeated-crash scans oracle-correct; 75/25 replay scheduling holds restart p99 ≤2× baseline.
Inject repeated crashes during 75/25 replay, compare recovered scans and commits to oracle, and measure restart scan p99 against baseline.
Run RepeatCrash-75: inject three crashes per split during 75/25 child replay; check committed keys, pinned scans, and restart scan p99.
RepeatCrash-75 bundle records three crash hooks per split, recovered-key and pinned-scan oracle comparisons, plus restart scan-p99 traces.
Reproduce RepeatCrash-75 across 1,000 triple-crash splits; audit recovered commits, pinned scans, map generations, and scan p99 against baselines.
RepeatCrash-75: 1,000 triple-crash splits had zero lost commits or scan mismatches; worst restart scan p99 was 1.94× baseline.
Adopt single-generation routing with mandatory parent redo and 75/25 replay I/O: triple-crash scans stayed correct at 1.94× p99.
